options.text: Breeding organisms that have been genetically modified
Choosing organisms with desirable characteristics to breed together
Allowing organisms to breed randomly in the wild
Cloning organisms to produce identical copies

questions.explanation: Selective breeding (artificial selection) is the process where humans choose organisms with desirable characteristics and breed them together over many generations to enhance those traits.

questions.stem: What is the first step in selective breeding?

options.text: Identify and select individuals with the desired characteristic
Modify the DNA of the organisms
Breed all organisms together randomly
Clone the best organism

questions.explanation: The first step in selective breeding is to identify the desired characteristic and then select individuals from the population that show this characteristic most strongly. These selected individuals are then bred together.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of selective breeding in animals?

options.text: A wolf hunting in the wild
Bacteria developing antibiotic resistance
Breeding cows that produce the most milk together
A frog evolving brighter colours

questions.explanation: Breeding cows with high milk yield together is an example of selective breeding. Farmers select the highest-yielding cows and breed them over many generations to increase milk production in the herd.

questions.stem: What is a major disadvantage of selective breeding?

options.text: It increases genetic variation
It reduces genetic variation, making populations vulnerable to disease
It cannot be used on plants
It takes only one generation

questions.explanation: Selective breeding reduces genetic variation because only organisms with similar desired characteristics are bred. This inbreeding can make populations more vulnerable to diseases and less able to adapt to environmental changes.

questions.stem: How does selective breeding differ from natural selection?

options.text: Natural selection is faster than selective breeding
There is no difference between them
In selective breeding, humans choose which organisms reproduce; in natural selection, the environment does
Selective breeding only works on plants

questions.explanation: In selective breeding, humans decide which organisms reproduce based on desired traits. In natural selection, the environment determines which organisms survive and reproduce based on how well their characteristics suit their surroundings.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of selective breeding in plants?

options.text: Weeds spreading across a field
A plant growing towards light
Developing wheat varieties with higher grain yield
Photosynthesis producing glucose

questions.explanation: Developing wheat varieties with higher grain yield is an example of selective breeding. Farmers have selectively bred wheat over thousands of years, choosing plants that produce more grain and are more disease-resistant.

options.text: The process of selecting the worst organisms to breed
When animals become sad from being kept in captivity
The reduced fitness and health problems caused by breeding closely related organisms
A type of mutation caused by selective breeding

questions.explanation: Inbreeding depression occurs when closely related organisms are bred together, increasing the chance that offspring inherit two copies of harmful recessive alleles. This leads to reduced fitness, health problems, and lower fertility.
